newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU collapse may lead to EU disintegration - Finland.
newsitem.headline: EMU collapse may lead to EU disintegration - Finland.

text.p: Economic and Monetary Union, due for kick-off in 1999, is so highly charged politically that failure may lead to disaster and force the European Union to drift towards disintegration, a Finnish government report said.
"Failure to implement EMU ... would represent a major political disaster," Finland said in the report, which the national parliament started to debate on Wednesday.
If EMU collapsed, it might "trigger a crisis which the EU in its present form would be unable to solve, drifting into disintegration," it said.

The alternatives to implementing EMU were to postpone it or give up the whole project. "Either course would be politically difficult, and would have a profound impact on the future of the Union," the report said.
The fate of the single currency would to a large extent determine the future course for the 15-member European Union.
"Implementation of the third phase of Economic and Monetary Union is a vital cornerstone of the internal market and stable economic development," it said
The third phase of the process towards a single currency should be implemented on schedule from the beginning of 1999, Finland said.
"Any wavering or delay in this process would have a detrimental effect on the stability of the financial markets, and on the future progress of the internal market," it said.
The report acknowledged that the fiscal austerity introduced to improve the resilience of public economies in the run-up to EMU had certain drawbacks.
"This has required and will continue to require adaptation and the attendant costs, one of which is unemployment," it said.
Finland is in favour of including as many nations as possible in the third phase provided that the convergence criteria are interpreted as intended in the Maastricht Treaty.
"The economies of the member states present substantial structural differences, which do not show any sign of narrowing despite all the remedial action taken or planned," Finland said.
EMU would divide the EU countries into at least two categories.
"The inner circle will enter the third phase of economic and monetary union and adopt a single currency," Finland said.
It did not list which countries it saw belonging to the inner circle, but said the Finnish economy was well on the way to meeting the convergence criteria.

The model for different speeds of integration would become institutionalised. Certain member states would proceed with more rapidly paced multi-core institutional arrangements, but such arrangements should not be permanent," Finland said.
Although failure to create EMU could prove fateful, the drive to meet the convergence criteria was important in itself.
"Irrespective of whether the third phase of EMU becomes a reality, greater predictability, economic stability and sound public finances are desirable aims in their own right," it said.
